name: China GDP per head, 1000-1850
method: Maddison Project Database 2020 (Bolt and van Zanden), GDP per capita in 2011 international dollars; China 1000-1850 from Broadberry, Guan and Li (2018), built from Song, Ming and Qing data on cultivated land, yields, crafts, government and population. No error bands are published; the authors treat early values as indicative, and Deng and O'Brien question the wage and price inputs.

name: Britain GDP per head, 1000-1913
method: Maddison Project Database 2020 (Bolt and van Zanden), GDP per capita in 2011 international dollars; England (Great Britain from 1700, UK later) from Broadberry et al. (2015) output-side national accounts. No bands published.

name: Netherlands GDP per head, 1400-1913
method: Maddison Project Database 2020 (Bolt and van Zanden), GDP per capita in 2011 international dollars; Holland and the Netherlands, national accounts reconstruction. No bands published.

name: Japan GDP per head, 1000-1913
method: Maddison Project Database 2020 (Bolt and van Zanden), GDP per capita in 2011 international dollars; Japan 730-1874 from Bassino, Broadberry, Fukao, Gupta and Takashima (2019), later years from Fukao et al. No bands published.

name: China population, 1000-1913
method: Maddison Project Database 2020 population column (thousands, converted to people); benchmark estimates for China built on registered counts adjusted for under-registration. Note the fall from 160 million (1600) to 138 million (1700) across the Ming-Qing transition and from 412 million (1850) to 358 million (1870) across the Taiping era.

name: Tang registered population, 755 and 760
method: Registered population in the Tang household registers as reported by Durand (1960). The fall measures the collapse of registration during the An Lushan war, not deaths; true population is unknown.

name: Taiping war deaths
method: Order-of-magnitude range: 20 million is the conservative figure most historians cite for deaths from war, famine and disease in 1850-64; 30 million the upper end of commonly cited estimates. County reconstructions of population loss run higher. No census exists.
